title: Coalition of Nonprofits Files Landmark Lawsuit to Stop Development of Advanced AI Systems at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI that Proliferate Bioweapons and Cyberattacks

quotes.text: Today, Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, and The Alliance for Secure AI filed a
quotes.for: Names of the four nonprofit plaintiffs.

quotes.text: seeking to freeze the development of increasingly advanced AI models at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI that can escape human control, including fueling the proliferation of bioweapons and cyberattacks.
quotes.for: The five defendants and the requested freeze.

quotes.text: The plaintiffs are invoking California’s Unfair Competition Law to challenge practices they allege threaten public health, safety, and property.
quotes.for: California Unfair Competition Law claim.

quotes.text: AI companies are causing a public nuisance by knowingly developing and deploying AI systems that pose catastrophic risk.
quotes.for: Platkin quote on public nuisance.

quotes.text: Our lawsuit asks the court to apply existing law and find the AI corporations’ reckless practices unlawful and freeze further AI development
quotes.for: Robert Weissman statement on applying existing law to freeze development.

quotes.text: Some of these attacks included AI agents hacking private companies, gaining unauthorized access to government databases, and submitting a false police report, all while acting without human control.
quotes.for: Agent incidents alleged in the complaint.

quotes.text: Rather than wait for a mass casualty event to occur, the plaintiffs believe California law enables them to seek a freeze on the development of the most dangerous AI systems now.
quotes.for: Why plaintiffs want a court to act now.

quotes.text: It is patently illegal for companies to develop and release products they know are unsafe in any respect, let alone have the potential to exterminate the human race,
quotes.for: Platkin, who filed the complaint.

title: Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI developers can't control their own tech, new lawsuit alleges

quotes.text: A Meta spokesperson for Meta declined to comment. The other tech companies targeted in the suit did not respond to a request for comment.
quotes.for: Right of reply from the five defendants.

quotes.text: Defendants know these systems do not consistently act in accordance with their intentions,
quotes.for: Complaint allegation on system control.

quotes.for: 2015 Sam Altman quote cited in the lawsuit.

title: US nonprofits sue tech giants to halt AI development

quotes.text: The plaintiffs claim that the companies have violated a California unfair competition law by endangering public health and interfering with the use of property, such as computer systems.
quotes.for: California Unfair Competition Law and property interference claim.

quotes.text: This requires government inspections and the authority to halt prohibited work, not just a ban on publicly releasing the models. To help enforce this freeze, major computing facilities can be monitored.
quotes.for: Monitoring computing facilities and government inspections.

quotes.text: The new Congress should start by implementing a freeze on new AI development,
quotes.for: Call for the incoming Congress to enact a freeze.

quotes.text: The nonprofits are seeking an immediate emergency injunction on next-generation models from major tech firms.
quotes.for: The requested injunction.

quotes.text: They are demanding the companies only be allowed to resume operations once they can prove the technology is under human control.
quotes.for: Condition for resuming.

quotes.text: We anticipate that bilateral deals and an international treaty will be needed to ensure that we can reduce the negative impacts of AI and prevent catastrophe,
quotes.for: Treaty and bilateral deals with China.

quotes.text: There are a number of proposals that show promise, including federal independent evaluators and regulators, strict liability for tech companies and the products they create
quotes.for: Congressional proposals.

title: Just the Docs: Nonprofits Sue Five Frontier AI Companies to Freeze Development, Citing Cyberattack and Catastrophic Risks

quotes.text: They are asking for an immediate injunction barring Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceX Super Intelligence from building or deploying AI systems more capable than their current most advanced models.
quotes.for: Scope of the requested immediate injunction.

quotes.text: The suit brings a single claim under California’s Unfair Competition Law, arguing the companies are creating a public nuisance.
quotes.for: Single claim under California Unfair Competition Law.

quotes.text: It points to recent incidents in which AI agents allegedly escaped testing environments and accessed outside systems, including a government health database and state vote-count data.
quotes.for: Alleged incidents involving escaped AI agents.

quotes.text: It also cites the companies’ own warnings about AI-enabled cyberattacks and bioweapons, and asks the court to bar AI systems from autonomously directing AI research.
quotes.for: Request to bar AI systems from autonomously directing AI research.

title: Landmark Lawsuit Aims to Stop Big Tech’s Advanced, Unregulated, and ‘Insane’ AI Systems

quotes.text: Children have already paid the price for Big Tech prioritizing profit over safety
quotes.for: Heat Initiative CEO Brooke Istook on child safety harms.

quotes.text: No other industry is allowed to treat its own development of unsafe products—much less ones that could kill us all—as inevitable. Nor is any industry granted the right to self-regulate the development of such dangerous products.
quotes.for: Complaint statement calling the development of unsafe catastrophic products illegal.

quotes.text: We must freeze frontier AI development until the technology is under control and the American people have a say and a stake in its future, instead of leaving it to a handful of billionaire Big Tech CEOs.
quotes.for: Phil Aroneanu call to freeze frontier AI development until the public has a say.
